executive_summary: Renewed Iranian aerial strikes on Bahrain and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have shattered a ten-week regional lull, locking Gulf states, the United States, and Iran into a high-stakes standoff over maritime chokepoint control and the terms of a broader war settlement. Late Saturday night, an Iranian aerial strike sparked a fire at a civilian industrial facility near Sitra Island in Bahrain while Bahrain Defense Force air defenses intercepted incoming projectiles—prompting Manama to invoke UN Security Council Resolution 2817 and rally immediate GCC collective security backing from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar. Concurrently, UKMTO verified two separate projectile strikes on outbound commercial tankers off Khasab, Oman, while Iranian forces claimed a third vessel hit a naval mine and broadcast footage of a new underground dual-missile launcher to signal sustained anti-access capability. These kinetic escalations reflect Tehran's effort to leverage chokepoint disruption in the Strait of Hormuz—alongside claimed strikes on U.S. Patriot air-defense radars at Al-Riffa and Awali in Bahrain—to compel Washington to lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports without surrendering Iran's 60%-enriched uranium stockpile abroad. Despite two hours of Qatari mediation in Tehran on Friday night, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Sunday that reopening Hormuz depends strictly on Washington accepting Tehran's preconditions, even as Qatar and Germany jointly demanded unimpeded maritime transit. Across adjacent theaters, Saudi-led coalition air defenses intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile near Mecca early Sunday following Saturday's interception of three ballistic missiles toward Riyadh and two drones in direct retaliation for renewed coalition strikes on Hodeidah port and Sanaa fuel storage, while sustained Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon coincided with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun's Independence Day demand for both an Israeli withdrawal and state monopoly over arms.

regional_sections.summary:
• Bahrain Under Sustained Pressure (Verified Official / Attributed): Bahrain's Interior Ministry confirmed an Iranian aerial strike sparked a fire at a civilian industrial facility late Saturday (near Sitra Island, home to Bapco refining infrastructure) with no casualties, while BDF air defenses intercepted incoming projectiles; the IRGC claimed strikes on two U.S. Patriot radar systems at Al-Riffa and Awali, continuing a pattern begun on 13 November after strikes on Iranian coastal infrastructure in Hormozgan.
• Hormuz Tanker Attrition (Verified Official / Attributed): UKMTO verified two separate projectile strikes on outbound tankers 11 NM north and 17 NM east of Khasab, Oman on Saturday with all crew safe, while Iranian state media claimed a vessel caught fire after striking a naval mine in a restricted zone and reported shooting down a U.S. drone over Qeshm Island.
• Diplomatic Deadlock (Attributed / Verified Official): Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi stated Sunday that reopening the Strait of Hormuz is 'not difficult' if Washington accepts Tehran's conditions while ruling out transferring Iran's 60%-enriched uranium abroad; Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed two hours of Qatari mediation in Tehran Friday night.

• Western Coast & Capital Defense (Verified Official): Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile targeting western Saudi Arabia (near Mecca and critical Red Sea export infrastructure at Yanbu) early Sunday, following Saturday's interception of three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and two drones alongside five Civil Defense alerts across Najran, Riyadh, Al-Sulayyil, and Jazan.
• Tit-for-Tat Escalation (Attributed / Corroborated): The missile launches followed renewed coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah port and Sanaa oil storage facilities, prompting Houthi warnings to commercial shipping to vacate Saudi Red Sea ports and declaring Saudi airspace unsafe.

• Lebanese Sovereignty Squeeze (Verified Official / Corroborated): Marking Lebanon's 83rd Independence Day, President Joseph Aoun demanded both a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon and an end to non-state armed groups (Hezbollah) operating outside Lebanese state authority, even as Israeli airstrikes and artillery fire continued across southern border towns (Kfar Tebnit, Mansouri, Majdal Zoun) with low-altitude drone activity over Beirut and Sidon.
• Syria & Israeli Coalition Dynamics (Corroborated): Turkish FM Hakan Fidan warned Sunday that Israeli military backing for Druze factions in southern Syria risks provoking clashes with Damascus's post-Assad administration and triggering a wider regional conflict, while Likud demanded retaining Israeli security zones in Gaza, Lebanon, and Syria during unity talks.

• UK FCDO & European Advisories: Strengthened regional travel warnings across 15 Middle Eastern states—including the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, and Turkey—citing heightened military unpredictability, aviation disruption, and elevated threat levels near commercial and tourist hubs.
• U.S. Department of State & Watch Indicators (Next 48–72 Hours): Maintains Level 4 (Do Not Travel) advisories for Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen with ordered-departure status active in Saudi Arabia; monitor whether Iranian salvos expand toward Gulf energy export terminals, UKMTO/JMIC transit alerts near Khasab, and follow-on Qatari shuttle diplomacy (@MOFAQatar_EN / @IRIMFA_SPOX).
